This page maps textbook balance quantities to the UpstreamDrift implementation audited at commit [`3afe09c1`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/commit/3afe09c1ed0247a459d16bf75cf0b28bb64f584a). It cites module paths only; it does not validate hardware walking performance.

## Frame and Validity

`ZMPComputer` (`src/robotics/locomotion/zmp_computer.py`) assumes a flat ground plane at `ground_height` (default $z=0$) with **$z$ up**. Center of pressure (CoP) equals ZMP on that plane. `ZMPResult.is_valid` is true only when the horizontal ZMP lies inside the supplied support polygon **and** CoM acceleration was not estimated by finite differences (see below).

## ZMP From Centroidal Kinematics

With CoM position $\mathbf{c}$, acceleration $\mathbf{a}_c$, angular-momentum rate $\dot{\mathbf{L}}_c$, mass $m$, and $z_{\mathrm{rel}} = c_z - z_{\mathrm{ground}}$, the code uses vertical denominator $d = a_{c,z} + g$. For $|d| < 10^{-6}$ it returns a free-fall result (`_free_fall_result`) instead of dividing.

Horizontal components match the module docstring in `compute_zmp`:

$$
x_{\mathrm{zmp}} = c_x - z_{\mathrm{rel}}\frac{a_{c,x}}{d} - \frac{\dot{L}_{c,y}}{m\,d},
\qquad
y_{\mathrm{zmp}} = c_y - z_{\mathrm{rel}}\frac{a_{c,y}}{d} + \frac{\dot{L}_{c,x}}{m\,d}.
$$

**Sign convention:** the $\dot{L}$ terms carry **no** factor of $z_{\mathrm{rel}}$; only the linear-acceleration terms do. The $y$ equation adds $\dot{L}_x$ where the $x$ equation subtracts $\dot{L}_y$—this matches the horizontal moment balance stated in the file header.

Total normal force is reported as $m(d) = m(a_{c,z}+g)$.

### Finite-Difference Acceleration

When `com_acceleration` is omitted, the class estimates it from velocity history and `dt`. In that case `is_valid` is forced **false** and `validity_reason` records the estimation caveat, even if the ZMP lies in the polygon.

### Default Support Polygon

If `support_polygon` is `None`, the code warns and uses a **origin-centred** rectangle $0.26\,\mathrm{m}\times 0.15\,\mathrm{m}$ (half-length $0.13\,\mathrm{m}$, half-width $0.075\,\mathrm{m}$). Feet away from the world origin therefore appear “out of support” unless a measured foot polygon is supplied (`_check_support`, ~lines 496–512).

## Capture Point and DCM

`compute_capture_point` and `compute_dcm` implement the LIPM scaling $\omega = \sqrt{g/z_{\mathrm{rel}}}$ with $z_{\mathrm{rel}} \leftarrow 0.01\,\mathrm{m}$ if non-positive. Horizontal capture point:

$$
\xi_x = c_x + \frac{\dot{c}_x}{\omega}, \qquad
\xi_y = c_y + \frac{\dot{c}_y}{\omega}.
$$

**Worked numeric check (code conventions):** $z_{\mathrm{rel}}=0.9\,\mathrm{m}$, $g=9.81\,\mathrm{m/s}^2$ gives $\omega \approx 3.30\,\mathrm{rad/s}$. With $\dot{c}_x=0.5\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $c_x=0$, $\xi_x \approx 0.151\,\mathrm{m}$ ahead—useful when auditing `stability_margin` signs.

## Centroidal MPC (Research Prototype)

`CentroidalMPC` (`src/research/mpc/specialized.py`) plans over a 9-state vector $[\mathbf{c}, \dot{\mathbf{c}}, \mathbf{L}_c]$ with contact forces at 1–4 points. Mass resolves from `get_total_mass()`, `total_mass`, or `mass` on the engine when present; otherwise it falls back to **`_DEFAULT_CENTROIDAL_MASS_KG = 50`**. Contact positions default to a biped-style spread along $y$ at fixed $x=0.1\,\mathrm{m}$.

The centroidal momentum matrix $A_G(q)$ used elsewhere appears on the `HumanoidCapable` protocol (`src/robotics/core/protocols.py`); this MPC layer uses the reduced lumped model above rather than a full $A_G$ assembly.
